stories.title: Mathematicians are amazed by ‘holy grail’ proof of Riemann hypothesis
stories.summary: An AI company claims to have used AI to prove the Riemann hypothesis, a nearly 200-year-old problem concerning prime number distribution. The proof is reportedly 250,000 pages long, with a 17-million-line version for proof-checking software. It has not yet been formally reviewed by other mathematicians, and the full proof has not been released.
stories.finding: An AI company claims to have used AI to prove the Riemann hypothesis, a nearly 200-year-old problem concerning prime number distribution. The proof is reportedly 250,000 pages long, with a 17-million-line version for proof-checking software. It has not yet been formally reviewed by other mathematicians, and the full proof has not been released.
stories.significance: If verified, proving the hypothesis would resolve a foundational question regarding prime number distribution and validate numerous dependent mathematical theorems.
stories.caveat: The proof spans millions of lines of code, has not been formally peer-reviewed, and could theoretically exploit an undiscovered software bug.

stories.title: Quantum effect could reverse gravity and violate Einstein’s theory of relativity
stories.summary: Two independent research teams mathematically modeled how quantum effects could theoretically make gravity repulsive, pushing objects apart instead of attracting them. This proposed phenomenon, which contradicts Einstein's theory of general relativity, could be tested in laboratory experiments using bacterium-sized objects that maintain a quantum superposition state, though such experiments are expected to be challenging.
stories.finding: Two independent research teams mathematically modeled how quantum effects could theoretically make gravity repulsive, pushing objects apart instead of attracting them. This proposed phenomenon, which contradicts Einstein's theory of general relativity, could be tested in laboratory experiments using bacterium-sized objects that maintain a quantum superposition state, though such experiments are expected to be challenging.
stories.significance: Demonstrating repulsive gravitational interactions in laboratory experiments could reveal whether gravity possesses inherently quantum properties, departing from general relativity.
stories.caveat: Lab tests will be exceptionally difficult because required bacterium-sized objects experience acceleration less than a quadrillionth of Earth's gravity.

stories.title: A brain region known for listening helps us speak
stories.summary: A small part of Wernicke's area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus, is active just before speech production, not just during comprehension. This finding, based on brain activity measurements and electrical stimulation in people, may inform efforts to restore speech using implanted devices.
stories.finding: A small part of Wernicke's area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus, is active just before speech production, not just during comprehension. This finding, based on brain activity measurements and electrical stimulation in people, may inform efforts to restore speech using implanted devices.
stories.significance: Clarifying how this auditory area contributes to speech could improve brain-computer interfaces aimed at restoring speech to individuals who cannot talk.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.
